story.value: The name chlorine comes from the Greek word chloros, meaning "pale green" or "greenish yellow".
Chlorine was discovered by the Swedish pharmacist and chemist Carl-Wilhelm Scheele in 1774.
In 1810, the English chemist Humphry Davy proved that chlorine was an element.

uses.value: Chlorine is used to make drinking water safe and to treat swimming pools.
Chlorine is commonly used as an antiseptic.
Sodium chloride, a chlorine compound commonly known as table salt, is used to season food.
Chlorine is used in the production of paper products, textiles and medicines.
